AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS
1. This DAR was filed on 03/09/2024 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 20/02/2024 in which one Sh. Devender Kumar S/o Sh. Mukesh Kumar (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per petitioner on 20/02/2024, he went to the shop of Neeraj at about 10.30 P.M on motorcycle bearing registration no. DL-5SD-7596 and on going to house on the aforesaid motorcycle which was PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2025.05.06 13:23:20 +0530 driven by him and at about 10.30 PM, he alongwith Neeraj crossed Barfkhana and going towards Pahari Dheeraj Road and reached near Church in the meantime one Chhota Hathi

bearing registration number DL-1LAG-1739 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") came from Hindu Rao Hospital, Delhi in a very most rash, negligent, reckless and zig-zag manner at a very high speed without any regard from the traffic rules and also tried to overtake but due to said illegal overtake the offending vehicle fell down over the motorcycle of the petitioner and due to heavy impact, the petitioner and Neeraj,
driver of the offending vehicle Chhota Hathi bearing registration no. DL-1LAG-1739.
It is further stated that R-1 left the spot leaving the said offending vehicle.
It is further stated that thereafter one TSR driver left the petitioner and Neeraj in Hindu Rao Hospital, Delhi for treatment.

It is further stated that the attending doctors of Hindu Rao Hospital, Delhi prepared the MLC bearing No.
777/2024 dated 20/02/2024.
It is further stated in the said accident, the petitioner has received the grievous injuries such as right leg fracture under knee, right let foot fracture and grievous injuries whole over body.
It is further stated that the said accident took place due to the sole negligence and carelessness of the R-.

It is further stated that he has spent Rs.50,000/- on his medical treatment,
Rs. 40,000/- on conveyance, Rs. 50,000/- on special diet and Rs.60,000/- on attendant.
He seeks compensation to the tune of Rs.60 Lakhs on account of the injuries sustained by him the vehicular accident.
It is further stated that at the time of accident he was 25 years of age and was doing private job of supply of parcels and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

11. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India)
Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,

sentences.text: In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner claims that he he was 25 years of age and was doing the private job of supplying of parcel and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The medical records placed on record by petitioner reflect that the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries which resulted into 32% permanent physical disability with to right lower limb.
The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that he was unable to resume his vocation since the date of accident.

In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner has become unfit for work for rest of his life after the accident and he could not have worked for about 06 months due to the injuries.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the Minimum Wages payable to a Matriculate Person in Delhi as on the date of accident.
Accordingly, the Minimum Wages admissible to a Matriculate Person as on 16/04/2023 in Delhi the earnings was Rs.21,215/-.

As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.1,27,290/-
(Rs.21,215/- X 6).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Loss of future earnings due to disability 16.
Petitioner claimed in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A that he has become permanently disabled after the accident and could not perform his work by resuming his duties.

As per disability PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2025.05.06 13:23:53 +0530 certificate, the petitioner has suffered 32%
permanent physical impairment with respect to right lower limb which is non progressive and not likely to improve in future.

Since, the petitioner was working as a Porter for supplying parcels by using his motorcycle and was earning handsomely, however, after the accident due to 32%
permanent physical impairment in relation to his right lower limb he is forced to work as a helper in a factory of manufacturing cookers.
As per petitioner his income has been reduced to almost half.
Apparently, due to the permanent disability the petitioner has to work as a helper thereby his work profile has been diminished.
The said transition has been caused due to the permanent disability due to accident.
Not only his work profile has been diminished but his salary has been reduced to almost half.
Considering this permanent disability in the background of changed work profile and earnings it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be taken as 32%.
This Tribunal has already assumed the monthly income of petitioner to be Rs.21,215/- at the relevant time.

As far as the age of petitioner at the time of accident is concerned, we may look into the photocopy of petitioner's Aadhar Card which is Ex. PW1/4, as per the said document, the date of birth of petitioner was 08/07/1998.
The date of accident is 20/02/2024.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident was around 25 years.
Therefore, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs.

Delhi Transport Corporation &
Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India)
Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
12.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
In view of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, it could be safely assumed that the petitioner has become unfit for work for rest of his life after the accident and he could not have worked for about 06 months due to the injuries.
In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the Minimum Wages payable to a Matriculate Person in Delhi as on the date of accident.
Apparently, due to the permanent disability the petitioner has to work as a helper thereby his work profile has been diminished.
Not only his work profile has been diminished but his salary has been reduced to almost half.
Considering this permanent disability in the background of changed work profile and earnings it would be appropriate to hold that the functional disability of petitioner be taken as 32%.
